$what: Provenance of act_descriptor.emp — aeon's OJZ act 1 level descriptor, vendored VERBATIM at a named aeon revision so that Aurora's rule-4 constant reader is exercised against aeon's real text and not against a hand-written sample. The five per-row `ensure` predicates inside `ojz_region(...)` are rule 4 of the regions contract, and the constants they name (REGION_MIN_SPAN, CENTRE_X_MIN/MAX, CENTRE_Y_MIN/MAX) are DERIVED here, in a chain whose leaves live in engine/system/constants.emp — vendored beside this file as engine_constants.emp at a revision that agrees.
$why_the_whole_file_and_not_the_20_lines: A trimmed fixture is a hand-written one, and it would certify the reader against a text no build ever sees. The whole file carries what actually makes this parsing hard: `const` inside prose comments, `if DEBUG == 1 { … } else { … }` initializers, two different widths (ACT_W and OJZ_AUTHORED_ACT_W), and names declared far from where they are used. Reading it whole is the only way a green row means the reader survives aeon's bytes.
$not_the_same_file_as: test/fixtures/effects/raster-owners/section-mode/act_descriptor.emp, which is an older trimmed copy with no provenance sidecar, kept for the raster-owners rows. That one is NOT pinned and must not be used to answer a question about aeon's current text.
